name: Putting mascara, kohl, aloe, honey or breast milk in babies' eyes
what_people_do: Apply mascara-type eye cosmetics to a newborn's eyes, or instil aloe, honey, plant sap or breast milk for red or sore eyes.
why_they_say_it_works: To "clear" or strengthen the eyes and treat redness.

documented_by.source: Udigwe GO, Emelumadu OF, Udigwe IB 2013, West Afr J Med, PMID 24488282
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Nnewi, 330 Igbo mothers: 28.5% regularly applied mascara to their babies' eyes to "clear" the eyes.

documented_by.source: Traditional Eye Medicine in Rural Somalia, 2026, Clin Ophthalmol, PMID 41907805 (commentary)
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Rural Somalia (commentary): traditional eye medicine includes aloe, expressed breast milk, honey and tree sap for redness, light sensitivity and pain; case reports and observational studies link it with worse corneal disease.

evidence.tested: Traditional eye remedies and corneal disease
evidence.population: Case reports and observational studies cited in a commentary
evidence.finding: Associated with microbial keratitis, corneal scarring and plant-sap toxic keratoconjunctivitis; primary studies not read.

source.name: Traditional Eye Medicine in Rural Somalia, 2026, Clin Ophthalmol, PMID 41907805 (commentary)

harm_note: The ocular surface is easily infected or scarred; "natural does not mean sterile". Seek an eye clinic for any red or painful eye.
gaps: Primary Somali case series not read.
